consensus_summary: Consensus primary sense is divine teaching/guidance (esp. torah as revealed will/law and musar as formative discipline), God's word that imparts wisdom, righteousness, and the path of life; common alternatives are chastening, the Mosaic Torah as tutor, parental admonition, or associated metaphors (light/path). Treated as theological concept more than fixed symbol; no single emblematic code beyond that range.
book_summary: The discipline of the law, received and kept — what only fools despise.
consensus_core_identification: divine teaching/discipline (torah/musar) that forms wisdom and righteous living
book_core_identification: the discipline of the law when received and kept (despised only by fools)
boundary_disagreement: Book restricts the referent to the law's discipline specifically under the condition of being received and kept, whereas consensus admits broader divine teaching, Scripture generally, parental instruction, and Spirit guidance without that reception/keeping condition as definitional.
rationale: Both cores stay inside the same category of divine/law-related instruction and discipline (musar/torah), and the book directly reuses the fools-despise language of Prov 1:7 that consensus also cites. The book nonetheless materially narrows extension and precision by equating instruction with the kept discipline of the law rather than the wider pedagogical concept of divine teaching, thereby excluding some cases consensus includes while retaining the central referent.
strongest_objection: Consensus regularly treats instruction as a broader lexical-theological range (teaching + discipline + Torah + parental/apostolic forms) rather than exclusively the received-and-kept discipline of the law.
